method: Private offline Acorn AST examination of all 144 captured JavaScript bundles; independently scoped function-body member access and assignment classification. No captured code published.

structural_candidates.criteria: A candidate contains certain literal member-property pairs or explicit assignment to tracked graph/identity member properties; this is a filter, not a chat function classification.

supported_findings: The captured JavaScript includes syntactic functions that refer to both conversationId and messageId member properties.
Some independently scoped functions access mapping and selected-node-like member fields together.
Captured functions include explicit parent and children member writes, but these are not yet attributed to the ChatGPT message model.
These sites supply concrete targets for tracing callers, callees, argument shapes, and UI/network consumers within the captured bundles.
unresolved: Which of these functions belong to chat code rather than embedded third-party tree, editor or UI libraries?
Which exact source functions implement message ancestry, selected branch traversal, editing or regeneration?
Are graph fields reads, writes, or conversions of transport/export data, and how are they called from UI actions?
Which request parsers and streaming handlers pass data to those functions?
How do minification, aliases and dynamic imports limit call ownership conclusions?
limitations: Aggregates cover all saved JavaScript, including vendored libraries.
Source property co-occurrence is a syntactic observation, not proof of domain object identity.
Arrow and ordinary functions are counted separately; nested function bodies are excluded from their parents' local field analysis.
Property names are allowlisted technical vocabulary; actual objects, source names, source spans and literal values are never published.
Not a reconstructed call graph, observed runtime trace or verified server schema.
